blocks.text: The pattern set out in Judges 2 helps readers recognize recurring elements in the central narratives: Israel turns from the LORD, experiences distress, cries out, and is delivered. Yet the individual episodes are not mechanically identical, and they do not all include every stage in the same form. This helps explain why Judges 10 develops the familiar movement of wrongdoing, oppression, confession, and renewed crisis in its own distinctive way.
